newsitem.title: JAPAN: Venalum Japan aluminium shipments resume -- sources.
newsitem.headline: Venalum Japan aluminium shipments resume -- sources.

text.p: Venezuela's state-owned aluminium refinery Venalum resumed ingot shipments to Japan in October, in line with an agreement reached in late September with its Japanese minority shareholders, Japanese industry sources said on Wednesday.
The Venezuelan side halted shipments to Japan at the beginning of this year amid a dispute regarding the Japanese shareholders' veto rights.
An equity agreement between the two sides stipulates aluminium ingot shipments to Japan of 90,000 tonnes per year, although Japan's supply contract expired in December 1995.
The sources said monthly shipments began in October and would continue through March at an accelerated pace, to make up for quantities of ingot lost during the period when shipments were suspended.
Shipments would subsequently return to the monthly levels seen before this year's suspension, they added.
One industry source said the stepped-up shipments were spread out through next March in order to minimise any impact on the Japanese physical market for primary aluminium.
Traders doubted there would be any significant impact on Japanese aluminium premiums as a result of the shipments.

The industry source added that no agreement had yet been reached on the Japanese minority's veto powers over Venalum decisions. The Venezuelan government wants those powers reduced before the facility's expected privatisation next year.
